title: Number of Common Factors
description:
# Number of Common Factors

Given two positive integers `a` and `b`, return the number of **common factors** of `a` and `b`.

A positive integer `x` is a common factor when both `a % x == 0` and `b % x == 0`.

Return only the count, not the list of factors.

## Example 1

**Input:** a = 12, b = 6
**Output:** 4
**Explanation:** The common factors are `1`, `2`, `3`, and `6`.

## Example 2

**Input:** a = 25, b = 30
**Output:** 2
**Explanation:** The common factors are `1` and `5`.

## Constraints

* `1 <= a, b <= 1000`

solutions.name: Enumerate Up To Minimum
solutions.description:
## Approach

Every common factor must be at most `min(a, b)`. Scan every candidate from `1` through that limit and count it only when it divides both numbers.

## Key Insight

This is the direct translation of the definition. It is intentionally simple and is a good first solution before using `gcd` or factor-pair counting.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(min(a,b))
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Divisor Set Of Smaller Number
solutions.description:
## Approach

Enumerate factor pairs of the smaller number and store every divisor in a set. Then count the stored divisors that also divide the larger number.

## Key Insight

A factor pair `d` and `n / d` is discovered together, so scanning only up to the square root can still recover all divisors of the smaller number. The set also avoids double-counting when the smaller number is a perfect square.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(sqrt(min(a,b)))
- Space Complexity: O(sqrt(min(a,b)))

solutions.name: Enumerate Factors Of GCD
solutions.description:
## Approach

First compute `gcd(a, b)`. The common factors of `a` and `b` are exactly the factors of this gcd, so count the gcd's factor pairs up to its square root.

## Key Insight

The gcd compresses the problem to one number. When `factor` divides `g`, both `factor` and `g / factor` are divisors; count one or two depending on whether they are the same value.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(sqrt(gcd(a,b)))
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Prime Factor Count Of GCD
solutions.description:
## Approach

Compute `gcd(a, b)`, factorize it into prime powers, and apply the divisor-count formula. If the prime exponents are `e1`, `e2`, and so on, the number of divisors is `(e1 + 1) * (e2 + 1) * ...`.

## Key Insight

This route teaches the number-theory structure behind the count. It is more abstract than pair enumeration, but it scales the idea to larger divisor-count problems.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(sqrt(gcd(a,b)))
- Space Complexity: O(1)
